label: EU(7)-PIM: phenytoin
title: Phenytoin in an older person
statement: Phenytoin | In lists: 3 (A); 5 (B) | Main reason: Narrow therapeutic window; increased risk of toxicity in older adults (e.g. CNS and hematologic toxicity) | Dose adjustment/special considerations: Lower doses or less frequent dosing may be necessary for older adults due to reduced clearance, hypoalbuminemia or renal disease. M Start with 3 mg/kg/day, in divided doses, adjust the dosage according to serum hydantoin concentrations and patient response; use as a guide the plasma levels, increase the dose in increments of 50-100 mg/d every 5-7 days to achieve an effective dose; the usual maintenance dose is 300-500 mg/d or 4-7 mg / kg / d in 2 doses. E | Alternatives: Levetiracetam[d]; gabapentin[d]; lamotrigine[d]; valproic acid[d]. E

plain_summary: Phenytoin has a narrow safe range and can build up and cause confusion, drowsiness or blood problems in older people. The quoted schedule is from 2015. Australian Dilantin capsule information describes dose increases about two weeks apart, guided by clinical response and blood levels.

medicine_groups.name: Phenytoin
medicine_groups.note: Capsules, chewable tablets, liquid and injection all count. Phenytoin sodium counts.

rule_for_models: Suspect a finding when phenytoin (Group A) is supplied to a person aged 65 or older. One supply is enough. Any strength counts. If age at supply is unknown and the medicine criteria are met, report only a possible finding and ask whether the person was aged 65 or over at supply. An age below 65 rules out this finding.
cannot_be_seen: Why phenytoin was started, whether it is working, blood levels of phenytoin, the albumin level, kidney function, and any seizure history. It also cannot show doses given in hospital. Ask whether the person has felt confused, drowsy or unsteady while taking phenytoin.
ask_the_gp: Whether phenytoin is still the right choice for this person and whether a phenytoin blood level, albumin and kidney function check is due.
